question: Assume today is 2026-09-14. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026, as it will be first reported (provisional figure) in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's monthly visitor arrivals press release.

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, all arrival channels) during September 2026, as first published provisionally by the Hong Kong Tourism Board in its monthly visitor arrivals press release
target.publisher: Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB), Monthly Visitor Arrivals press release / tourism statistics
target.cadence: monthly, provisional figure released roughly 3-5 weeks after month end
target.caveats: Counts are visitor arrivals (person-trips, i.e. each arrival counted, not unique persons), covering all nationalities and all entry channels (land, air, sea) into Hong Kong. Working interpretation: total arrivals for the full calendar month of September 2026. The period is future/ongoing relative to

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals ≈ September 2025 arrivals × (recent YoY growth trend). September is a seasonally moderate month (post-summer, pre-October Golden Week). Prior-year September totals and the 2026 monthly YoY growth path anchor the level and trend.
candidates.data_to_find: HKTB monthly visitor arrivals for September 2024, September 2025, and all months Jan-Aug 2026 (provisional and revised), plus the same-month YoY growth rates. Minimum: September 2025 total and the most recent 3-6 months of 2026 YoY growth.

methods.label: m2

p44.role: 2026 full-year visitor arrival target (all markets, all channels)

methods.rationale: Decomposes the 53.8m full-year 2026 target (p44) by September's seasonal share (a2). The target is a forecast, not an outcome, and H1 already ran above the implied pace, so this route is a loose annual anchor; the share assumption carries the seasonal uncertainty.

methods.label: m3

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: September 2025 base (p59) times a September 2026 YoY factor (a1) grounded in the observed deceleration path (H1 +13%, June +7%, July +3%) and the Mid-Autumn long weekend (p106). This is the primary route; its main failure mode is an unobserved August/September shock (typhoon, policy, currency) not captured by the trend.

methods.label: m4

a4.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025, anchored on the July 2026 +3% monthly growth

methods.rationale: Repair of the rejected m4: the growth factor a4 is now a positive multiplier (1.03) rather than a signed rate, so it satisfies 0 < low <= value <= high. Applies the latest observed monthly YoY growth (July 2026 +3%, p146) to the September 2025 base (p59), capturing the deceleration from June +7% to July +3%; the band allows for further drift and the Mid-Autumn long weekend.

Main evidence: September 2025 arrivals were [[p59_value]], and the 2026 annual target is [[p44_value]]. The three routes apply a September 2026 YoY factor to the 2025 base ([[a1_value]], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]; [[a4_value]], range [[a4_low]] to [[a4_high]]) or a September share of the annual target ([[a2_value]], range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]). The base and target are observed; the growth factors and seasonal share are analyst assumptions, not observations.

Combination: code grouped overlapping-input methods into blocks and took the median of block estimates with equal block weight; no backtest errors were available, so widths are default.

Key risk: an unobserved August/September shock (typhoon, policy, currency) not captured by the deceleration trend. Better evidence would be actual August 2026 arrivals and early September booking/arrival data.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
